text: Large Language Models, or LLMs, are computer programs trained on massive amounts of text from books, websites, and articles. They work by predicting the next word in a sequence, learning patterns and relationships between words. This training helps them understand context and generate coherent responses. When you use an LLM, you give it a prompt, which is your instruction or question. The quality of the answer often depends on how clear and specific your prompt is, a skill called prompt engineering. These models can write essays, summarize texts, or even code. However, they have limits: they can confidently state false information, and they cannot truly reason or understand the world. They simply mimic patterns from their training data, so they may struggle with recent events or complex logic.
